verifications.claim: Artemis III is currently scheduled to launch in mid-2027.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: targeted launch in mid-2027 (planned)[3][1]"; "As of February 2026, NASA expects Artemis III to launch in mid-2027.[3][1]"; R3: "Launch: 2027"
verifications.reasoning: R1 directly states mid-2027 as the targeted and expected launch date; R3 confirms 2027.

verifications.claim: Artemis III will involve a crewed flight to low-Earth orbit to test docking capabilities between the Orion spacecraft and commercial lunar landers (SpaceX Starship or Blue Origin Blue Moon).
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: "Crewed Earth orbital Orion/HLS flight"; "rendezvous in Earth orbit with ... SpaceX's Starship HLS and Blue Origin's Blue Moon"; "test rendezvous and docking"; R2: "test ... in low Earth orbit"; R3: "low Earth orbit will test ... Orion ... and one or both commercial landers from SpaceX and Blue Origin"; R6: "to space ... In Earth orbit, Orion will rendezvous with one or both of NASA’s Human Landing Systems ... SpaceX and Blue Origin"
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources confirm crewed Earth/low-Earth orbit mission testing docking with specified landers; R1 notes LEO/HEO consideration but supports LEO as primary.

verifications.claim: The first human landing is now slated for Artemis IV in 2028.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: "Artemis IV tentatively designated as the first crewed lunar landing mission ... scheduled for 2028"; R2: "targeting an Artemis 4 liftoff in 2028 as the program's first crewed lunar landing"
verifications.reasoning: Both sources directly state Artemis IV as first crewed landing in 2028.

verifications.claim: Mission goal of Artemis III is to test rendezvous and docking of the crewed Orion capsule with commercial moon landers in Earth orbit.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: "The mission will rendezvous in Earth orbit with ... Human Landing System (HLS) vehicles ... test rendezvous and docking operations"; R2: "use Artemis 3 as a safe proving ground for those procedures [rendezvous and dock with Orion] in low Earth orbit"; R3: "test rendezvous and docking capabilities between Orion and ... commercial spacecraft"; R6: "test the docking capabilities ... in Earth orbit"
verifications.reasoning: Direct support across sources for Earth orbit rendezvous/docking test with Orion and commercial landers.

verifications.claim: Artemis III will be launched by NASA's Space Launch System (SLS) from Kennedy Space Center.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: "launch aboard the Space Launch System (SLS) rocket ... Launch site Kennedy, LC-39B"; R3: "launch in Orion on the SLS ... from NASA’s Kennedy Space Center"
verifications.reasoning: Exact match on SLS from Kennedy Space Center.

verifications.claim: The crewed landing on the Moon has been deferred to later missions (Artemis IV or V in 2028).
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: "Artemis IV tentatively designated as the first crewed lunar landing mission ... 2028"; R2: "Artemis 4 liftoff in 2028 as ... first crewed lunar landing, with the potential for Artemis 5 to repeat the feat later that same year"
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm deferral to Artemis IV in 2028, with R2 noting potential for V same year.

verifications.claim: Crew for Artemis III is not yet announced.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: "NASA administrator Jared Isaacman stated that the Artemis III crew will be revealed in the near future"; R6: "Reports this week also suggest that the crew selection process is underway, though NASA has not verified those claims"
verifications.reasoning: Sources indicate crew not yet announced/revealed, only future/planned.

verifications.claim: Selection of crew for Artemis III is underway.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: R1: "the Artemis III crew will be revealed in the near future"; R6: "reports this week also suggest that the crew selection process is underway, though NASA has not verified those claims"
verifications.reasoning: Implied by future reveal and unverified reports, but not directly confirmed by NASA.

verifications.claim: As of April 2026, NASA has revised the Artemis 3 mission profile to focus on orbital rendezvous rather than a direct lunar surface landing.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: "As of April 2026, NASA had not finalized the mission's orbital profile ..."; but earlier "On February 27, 2026 ... revised plan for Artemis III to perform tests with one or both landers in Earth orbit"; "In February 2026, the mission plan was revised to be a crewed test in Earth orbit"
verifications.reasoning: Revision to orbital focus occurred by Feb 2026, in place as of April 2026 per timeline.

verifications.claim: The revision follows an announcement by NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman on February 27, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: "On February 27, 2026, NASA administrator Jared Isaacman confirmed a revised plan"; R2: "Isaacman said. 'This is just not the right pathway forward'"
verifications.reasoning: Direct attribution of announcement to Isaacman on exact date.
